text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD#54321 fired - service=redis-prod-cluster - symptom=client connection storm / accept_queue spike - severity=critical

pagerduty: PD#54321 assigned to Lee (oncall).

Lee: acked PD#54321. I'm on it, looking at Grafana and k8s.

Maya: Grafana - redis-03 accept_queue=1900, connected_clients=4200, client_longest_output_list=350. Avg cmd latency for SET/INCR ~350ms. replication offset delta rising.

Sam: saw pgbouncer connections climbing too, pg write latency climbing ~400ms. Probably cascading retries from cache misses/fails.

Priya: initial hypothesis: scheduled batch workers (indexer-v2) started at 03:00 UTC after deploy, many ephemeral pods opening sockets without pooling — we've seen this pattern before.

Lee: can someone list top client IPs on redis-03? running client list now.

Sam: run this to group by addr:
```bash
redis-cli -h redis-03 CLIENT LIST | tr ' ' '\n' | grep addr | cut -d= -f2 | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 20
```

Maya: output: top 3 addrs are all in 10.16.32.0/21 (cluster for indexer-v2 autoscale). counts: 1820, 940, 420. basically the batch pool.

Lee: confirms noisy autoscale. Immediate mitigation: throttle or reject connections from that CIDR at the gateway or k8s network layer, and enable soft-fail for non-critical write paths. Sam can you flip gateway backoff?

Sam: on it. creating a temporary rate-limit rule for src_cidr=10.16.32.0/21, route=/api/v1/events and /sync -> 50 rps per pod, 429 backoff. Pushing change now.

Sam: applying rule via infra-console CLI:
```bash
infractl gateway update --name api-gw-prod --add-rate-limit 'src_cidr=10.16.32.0/21;path=/api/v1/events,/sync;rate=50s;burst=100;status=429'
```

ops-bot: runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/redis-connection-stampede (recommended actions: throttle upstream, identify offending deployment, restart batch pods, consider CLIENT KILL for abusive sockets).

Priya: recommend also flipping feature-flag to disable non-essential writes from indexer (ff: indexer_write_enabled=false), low risk and reduces write pressure. Can we do that now?

Lee: Priya go ahead once Sam confirms gateway rule is live.

Sam: gateway rule active :white_check_mark: traffic dropping to the rate-limit for the top CIDR. Accept_queue on redis-03 falling from 1900 -> 700 within 60s. latency trending down.

Maya: nice. pgbouncer connection churn decreasing, postgres write latency down to ~120ms. replication lag stabilizing.

Priya: feature flag turned off for indexer-v2 write paths. Confirmed jobs enter no-op mode.

Lee: good. we'll keep the throttle in place for 30 min then re-evaluate. Need to drain the existing noisy sockets — doing controlled CLIENT KILL for the worst offenders to free queues.

Sam: command I'm running (will target the top N sockets from that CIDR):
```bash
redis-cli -h redis-03 CLIENT LIST | grep 'addr=10.16.32' | awk -F 'id=' '{print $2}' | cut -d' ' -f1 | xargs -n1 -I{} redis-cli -h redis-03 CLIENT KILL id={}
```

Maya: after kill, accept_queue down to ~120, connected_clients 900. latency p50/p99 improving.

Lee: posting customer impact summary for PG/Oncall channel: some customers experienced 5xx for write endpoints, approx 2.3k requests failed during spike window (03:00-03:07 UTC). No data loss detected; writes retried by clients later.

Priya: note to support: affected endpoints /api/v1/events and /sync — advise customers to retry, and we've flagged the incident for postmortem.

Sam: paging escalation: keeping PD#54321 open until we confirm stability and rollback plan for indexer autoscale config.

ops-bot: handoff checklist posted to thread: https://runbooks.internal/redis-connection-stampede/checklist

Lee: passing to Priya for incident lead while I run retrospective config changes (limiting indexer pod concurrency, add jitter to start times). Priya, you own the post-incident comms and next actions.

Priya: ack — I'll coordinate with growth team to adjust schedule, and open a ticket for platform to implement per-deployment egress rate-limits and connection pooling guidance.

Sam: short-term followups: keep gateway throttle, adjust indexer max_concurrency from 200 -> 20, add startup spread 0-5m. Long-term: implement connection pooling SDK for batch workers, and add alert to detect CIDR-sourced client storms.

Maya: monitoring note: add a Grafana panel for accept_queue per node with top client CIDR breakdown, and add an alert if > 500 and top-cidr > 50% of clients.

Lee: thanks team. I'll keep PD open for another 45m and then close if stable. Great coordination. :heart:
